theories.name: Entropic Vacuum Rigidity (EVR)
theories.core_claim: Vacuum fluctuations contribute to gravity not through their energy but through their information-theoretic rigidity—the resistance of the vacuum state to deformation under acceleration. The equivalence principle applies to this rigidity, not to zero-point energy, explaining why Casimir energy gravitates while the absolute vacuum does not.
theories.mechanism: Drawing on the Unruh effect and entropic gravity, the gravitational response to a vacuum configuration is proportional to the Kullback-Leibler divergence D_KL(ρ_vac||ρ_accel), where ρ_vac is the vacuum state and ρ_accel is the Rindler thermal state seen by an accelerated observer. For uniform acceleration, this reduces to the standard Unruh temperature. For non-uniform fields (e.g., near Casimir plates), the spatial variation in this divergence sources curvature. The absolute zero-point energy cancels in the divergence, but energy differences (Casimir effect) produce non-zero divergence gradients.

theories.name: Scale-Dependent Degravitation Filter (SDDF)
theories.core_claim: Gravity acts as a high-pass filter on vacuum energy, but with a scale-dependent cutoff: wavelengths longer than the causal horizon at a given epoch do not contribute to the local stress-energy tensor, while shorter wavelengths (including Casimir modes) couple normally. This is not a modification of gravity but a statement about which modes are 'prepared' in the quantum state.
theories.mechanism: The graviton propagator is modified by a form factor Π(k²) = 1 - (1 + k²/Λ²)^{-β}, where Λ ~ H_0 and β > 0. For k >> Λ (Casimir modes, atomic scales), Π → 1 and coupling is normal. For k << Λ (cosmological zero-point modes), Π → 0 and coupling vanishes. The equivalence principle holds mode-by-mode: each mode gravitates proportionally to its energy, but the infinite tower of infrared modes decouples. The cosmological constant is small because the integral over unfiltered modes is finite and naturally O(H_0²M_Pl²).

theories.name: Scale-dependent coupling of vacuum fluctuations to gravity
theories.description: Vacuum fluctuations do couple to gravity, but only above a certain energy or length scale where quantum field theory in curved spacetime is valid. Below this scale (e.g., Planck scale), the absolute value of zero-point energy is not physically meaningful because it is renormalized away in flat spacetime. Gravity only responds to differences in energy density because the absolute value is an artifact of the theory's UV incompleteness. The equivalence principle applies to renormalized stress-energy, not bare zero-point energies.

theories.name: Contextual equivalence principle for vacuum energy
theories.description: The equivalence principle applies to vacuum fluctuations only in local inertial frames where the energy-momentum tensor is evaluated relative to the local vacuum state. In globally defined spacetimes, the absolute value of zero-point energy is ambiguous due to the choice of vacuum state (e.g., Minkowski vs. Rindler). Both sides are correct: gravity couples to differences in energy density when comparing different vacuum states, but within a single vacuum state, the equivalence principle holds for fluctuations relative to that vacuum. The hidden variable is the choice of vacuum state, which is observer-dependent.
theories.hidden_variable: The choice of vacuum state (e.g., Boulware, Hartle-Hawking, Unruh) which determines the zero-point energy baseline.

theories.description: Dark matter is a manifestation of vacuum fluctuations that have undergone a phase transition, forming a coherent condensate that couples to gravity via differences in energy density. In the early universe, vacuum fluctuations were uniform and did not gravitate (absolute value irrelevant). After symmetry breaking, topological defects or condensates formed, creating localized differences in vacuum energy that now act as dark matter. Both sides are correct: vacuum fluctuations do not gravitate in their symmetric phase, but their broken-symmetry remnants do, explaining why dark matter appears to interact only gravitationally.
theories.hidden_variable: The phase of the quantum vacuum (symmetric vs. broken symmetry) that determines whether vacuum fluctuations are uniform or form localized energy density differences.
theories.testable_prediction: If dark matter is a vacuum fluctuation condensate, it should exhibit scalar field-like behavior with a specific equation of state that transitions from w=-1 (uniform vacuum) to w=0 (pressureless matter) at a critical redshift. hypotheses.description: Vacuum fluctuations couple to gravity through an entropic rigidity mechanism where zero-point energy contributes to spacetime curvature via information-theoretic constraints on the quantum vacuum. The equivalence principle emerges from the thermodynamic cost of distinguishing inertial frames, with vacuum energy gravitating through a modified stress-energy tensor that includes entropic pressure terms.

The chameleon mechanism dynamically screens vacuum energy in low-density environments, explaining why zero-point energy does not produce observed large-scale curvature.

hypotheses.title: Scale-Dependent Degravitation Filter (SDDF)
hypotheses.description: Gravity acts as a high-pass filter on energy density, responding only to spatial variations and gradients while filtering out homogeneous vacuum contributions. The degravitation scale emerges from nonlocal infrared modifications to general relativity, with the cosmological constant problem solved by making the graviton effectively massive at Hubble scales.

hypotheses.title: Differential Entanglement Curvature (DEC) Gravity
hypotheses.description: The gravitational response to vacuum energy depends on entanglement structure rather than local energy density. Only differences in vacuum entanglement entropy across causal horizons couple to curvature; homogeneous zero-point energy decouples because it lacks entanglement gradients. Gravity emerges from the quantum information geometry of the vacuum.

hypotheses.title: Vacuum Energy Differential Gravitation (VEDG)
hypotheses.description: Gravity responds exclusively to differences in energy density relative to a fiducial vacuum state, not to absolute values. The equivalence principle applies only to deviations from the vacuum baseline; zero-point energy cancels in all gravitational measurements by construction, analogous to gauge invariance in electromagnetism.

hypotheses.title: Causal Set Vacuum Asymmetry (CSVA)
hypotheses.description: Vacuum fluctuations couple to gravity only when they violate discrete spacetime symmetry: in causal set theory, ordered sprinklings of Planck-scale events generate a non-zero Lorentz-invariant energy density that gravitates, while continuum-limit symmetric vacuum energy remains inert. The cosmological constant scales with the discreteness scale l_p / L_H and is naturally suppressed by N^{-1/2} for N elements in a Hubble volume.

hypotheses.title: Stochastic Vacuum Decoherence Gravity (SVDG)
hypotheses.description: Gravity arises from the decoherence of superposed vacuum states, with only the variance in vacuum energy density (not its mean) coupling to spacetime curvature. In regions with coherent vacuum superposition, the equivalence principle is modified; in classical limits, only energy density differences are detectable. Predicts gravitationally-induced decoherence rates scaling with curvature variance.

hypotheses.title: Topological Vacuum Polarization (TVP)
hypotheses.description: Vacuum energy couples to gravity through topological invariants of the spacetime manifold, not local curvature. Zero-point energy gravitates only when it generates non-trivial Pontryagin or Euler classes; trivial topologies screen vacuum energy completely. The equivalence principle holds locally but fails globally for vacuum-dominated spacetimes, explaining dark energy as a topological Casimir effect.

hypotheses.title: Conformal Vacuum Sequestering (CVS)
hypotheses.description: Vacuum energy is conformally invariant and therefore decouples from the Einstein-Hilbert action through a field redefinition. Gravity responds only to the trace anomaly of the vacuum, making zero-point energy gravitationally inert unless conformal symmetry is broken by boundaries or temperature. The cosmological constant is a free parameter fixed by boundary conditions, not vacuum physics.
